title: Compactify component variants and autolayout cleanup for UI kit
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Reduce cognitive overhead and rendering complexity in the Figma UI kit by compacting seldom-used variant axes, normalizing auto-layout constraints, and applying a publish gating process. Scope: buttons, toggle groups, table row atoms, and chart legend atoms. Out of scope: full redesigns of components and any live-page layout changes in product files. Approach: 1) Inventory variants and usage frequency across files, 2) Define canonical variant axes and collapse redundant states into token-driven visual differences (color/spacing), 3) Normalize auto-layout constraints to single-axis sizing rules, 4) Create migration aliases for existing instances (rename tokens + annotate instances), 5) Publish behind a gated release with canary teams and a rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: Button and toggle families reduced to a maximum of 3 boolean variant axes (size, tone, state) across primary/secondary/ghost tokens
Auto-layout normalized: instances using horizontal + vertical mixed constraints audited; >90% converted to single-axis primary auto-layout with explicit min/max sizing
Design tokens updated and a migration alias map published so existing files don't break on library update
Figma publish includes a detailed changelog and migration notes and a single rollback publish prepared
Two internal teams perform canary adoption with documented feedback and no severity >P1 regressions
qa_checklist: Verify every button instance in our 3 canonical product files renders as expected after library update
Confirm table row density variants align with tokens and do not shift column widths unexpectedly
Run Figma plugin token-linter across files and resolve any token name collisions
Smoke test exported code snippets in storybook for affected components
Confirm Figma publish created a rollback version and that it restores previous component names
